neighbours.label: the word that links a consequence back to the event that caused it ('complications from', 'after effects of', 'injuries from')
fire: The patient developed complications from the infection last spring.
For years the region suffered the after effects of the long civil war.
My uncle passed away in 2015 from complications of diabetes.
Several workers were treated for injuries from the factory explosion.
Doctors warned about the long-term after effects of the virus.
The town was still recovering from the damage of the flood.
Older adults face more complications from influenza than teenagers do.
Veterans often live with the lingering effects of the war for decades.
quiet: The patient walked into the clinic on a rainy afternoon last spring.
For years the region was known for its long dry summers.
My uncle retired in 2015 and moved to the coast.
Several workers were promoted to new roles at the factory.
Doctors gathered in the hall for the annual medical conference.
The town held a parade on the first day of summer.
Older adults often enjoy gardening more than teenagers do.
Veterans marched together in the city parade on Sunday.
